data.narrative:
Vermeer, a Series A-stage Defense & Security company founded by Brian Streem, has raised $10M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 10 peers—2 public (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private entities spanning the same sector and stage, including Stark Defence, Castelion, Singularity, NODA AI, and Anduril Industries.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy base ($10M) and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A progression, yields $20M. Peer-median valuation across 4 same-sector, same-stage comparables produces $700M, derived from a range of $125M (NODA AI) to $4.0B (Stark Defence), with Castelion at $1.0B and Singularity at $400M.

The triangulated valuation range spans $17M (low) to $805M (high), with a median of $360M across both methods. The wide dispersion—a ~47x ratio between low and high—reflects material uncertainty in where Vermeer sits within the Defense & Security peer distribution. Stage-progression implies early-stage positioning, while peer-median suggests comparability to established frontier-defense entrants. Key uncertainties include differentiation within an increasingly dense cohort of early-stage defense-tech companies and the sustainability of valuations at the upper quartile of the peer set.
